title: Introduce delegated burst bank and lease-refund protocol for cross-tenant burst reuse
author: Anika Shah
description:
Motivation: Dedicated capacity occasionally experiences underutilized burst capacity in tenant pockets while other tenants hit short-term demand spikes. Current burst banking is per-tenant and conservative, leaving potential cross-tenant utilization on the table. This PR introduces a delegated burst bank and a lease-refund protocol that allows eligible tenants (donors) to delegate a portion of unused burst credits to a shared bank for short-term borrow by peers (borrowers). The donor receives a refundable lease token and proportional credit reimbursement if the delegated burst is not used after a configurable lease TTL. The goal is to improve cluster-wide utilization without violating tenant throughput guarantees or accounting correctness.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new controller (pkg/autoscaler/delegated_bank.go) that manages the lifecycle of delegated burst leases, including delegation, reclamation, and refund accounting.
- Implements a lease-refund protocol: when a delegate happens, a LeaseToken is minted and registered; borrow events decrement the shared bank and are correlated back to leases; if a lease expires unused, an automated refund credits the donor's reservation ledger.
- Exposes new telemetry signals for auditing and alerting: delegated_delegations_total, delegated_refunds_total, delegated_borrow_success, delegated_borrow_reject (reasons), delegated_lease_age_seconds_histogram.
- Integrates with existing quota and preemption logic: delegated credits are considered soft credits and will be reclaimed before hard reservation preemption. Borrowers are still subject to per-tenant SLA checks; donors are given configurable protection windows to avoid accidental throughput regressions.
- Provides a feature flag and rollout plan: feature flag delegatedBurstBank.enabled=false by default; canary rollout via Dedicated cluster tag.
- Adds simulation harness tests and an end-to-end integration in perf-canary that demonstrate ~6-9% cluster-wide token throughput improvement in bursty workloads with no measurable increase in tail latency for protected tenants.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- Delegations are optional and opt-in per-tenant via config; by default tenants do not delegate.
- Refunds are strictly accounting operations that update reservation ledgers; they do not create extra capacity beyond existing committed capacity.
- The controller performs conservative admission control: a global cap on delegated outstanding credits is enforced and per-donor max-delegation fraction is configurable.

Migration and rollout:
- Add feature flag and operator config (charts/redwood/values.yaml) to toggle the behavior.
- Start with metric-only mode (delegatedBurstBank.reportOnly=true) to collect signals for one week.
- Canary enablement for three Dedicated pools; monitor delegated_borrow_reject rate and donor_quota_reduction_alert.
- Full enablement after two successful canaries and SIG-Infra approval.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover controller state transitions and refund accounting (pkg/autoscaler/controller_test.go).
- Integration test exercises preemption interplay with delegated credits (tests/integration/delegated_bank_e2e.sh).
- Perf harness scenario added (perf-canary/scenarios/delegated-burst-reuse.json) with synthetic tenant mixes used in prior autoscaler work.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- The design favors eventual consistency: short windows may show transient donor ledger skew during high churn. Conservatism in borrowing rules reduces chance of noticeable regressions.
- We do not attempt strong cross-tenant fairness enforcement in this iteration; future work can add proportional donor incentives and SLA-weighted delegation.

Related work and references:
- RFC: docs/rfc/delegated-burst-bank.md (design, invariants, API sketch)
- Linear: ENG-4301 (design), ENG-4320 (canary plan)

Checklist:
- [x] Controller and core logic implemented
- [x] Telemetry + metric registration added
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Chart/config knobs and feature flag included
- [x] Perf scenario and simulation added

Notes for reviewers: watch for race conditions around simultaneous refund and reclaim paths; I included a bounded retry with backoff in the reclaim loop. The PR intentionally keeps the borrow admission conservative to avoid increasing preemption. If we want faster refunds we can decrease lease TTL; trade-offs documented in the RFC.

review_comments: Diego Mendez: Left a couple of notes on race around refund+reclaim. Suggest adding a monotonic ledger checkpoint to avoid double refunds. Also can we add a prometheus label for donor_tier to help debugging?

Priya Raman: Question - how do we prevent a malicious tenant from delegating then causing borrow storms? Please add circuit breaker metrics.

release_notes: Introduce optional delegated burst bank with lease-refund protocol to enable safe cross-tenant reuse of short-term unused burst credits. Feature is opt-in and behind a feature flag. Metrics and rollout plan included.
short_summary: Adds delegated burst bank controller, lease-refund protocol, telemetry, tests, and config for opt-in cross-tenant burst reuse to improve cluster utilization with conservative safety defaults.
